title: WoDX NPC
description: World of Darkness Expanded: NPC profiles, combat tactics, routines and reactions. On an NPC's turn WoDX weighs what it could do from its temperament, fears and the fight, then suggests a plan to the Storyteller or (in Auto) moves and attacks with an undo card. NPCs with a routine keep hour-by-hour places on the Chronicle clock, and WoDX: Reaction regions let watchers notice and react. NPCs who hear a player at work on the map (WoDX Interactables) react through the same card, and a place put on alarm stays so for an hour and wary until dusk, lighting its WoDX: Alert zones. Factions take a turn each week of world time, hunting grounds follow Herd and Domain, and a Masquerade breach spreads as a rumour, every result through the approval queue. WoDX: Trigger regions pass on what happens when someone walks in, and an Alert zone can carry the alarm to other places by bell, telephone, radio or runner. Private use only; not for distribution or sale. Followers take orders: a player tells an NPC that serves their character to follow, wait, guard, keep watch or go to someone; a hard order waits for the Storyteller. Players talk to NPCs from a topic menu: they target someone close by, press Talk and pick a topic, and the NPC answers with a line the Storyteller wrote on a talk sheet, or with stock talk suited to the era and to how they regard the character: greetings, gossip, rumours from the rumour network, news, work and the way, what a mortal notices about the character, small talk on feasts and weather, debts, farewells and remembering a visit, voices for kinds of people, and remarks and cries as they go about their day. Factions can be founded in play from their founders' own Backgrounds, by the Storyteller or at a player's request; players can run a faction and give its orders; a strained faction may split; factions end or fold into another, keep founding and ending years, rise or end with dated events, and use the spheres of their age from 1197 to the Future Darkness. Kinds of NPC are natural rivals by line and era (Garou and Kindred, Sabbat and Camarilla, the Inquisition and every monster): rivals who meet and know each other for what they are may come to blows. Animals have their own ways: strays, guard dogs, cats, rats, birds, horses, livestock, wolves, bears, boars and bats, each with its places, years and hours, herding, holding its patch or bolder when hungry, and shy of wraiths. Criminals, combatants and townsfolk of every era have theirs too: cutpurses and bandits who give up when beaten, levies who break when their captain falls, police who hold a line and shoot from cover, and children, gossips and informers who say nothing now and tell someone later. Supernatural NPCs follow their clan, tribe, kith, Tradition or creed: Nosferatu who stalk from the sewers, Toreador salons, caern warders who never give ground, Hierarchy legions, redcaps, Arcanum scholars and the imbued by creed, each where and when they belong. Scenes the Storyteller turns on fill with passers-by and animals of the year, who walk through, stop a while and leave; a vampire can lead one aside to feed. Every tie WoDX keeps shows on the sheet and in a family and lineage tree; secrets can be found and held as hooks in the Ledger or laid bare at court; the Storyteller sees why each NPC feels as they do; talk lines can need a trait such as Dominate 2. Each character has one Followers window for everyone who serves them, and when witnesses see a culprit, word of what they looked like goes round by the means of the year and fades. Passers-by each feel something and keep a spark of dreaming that wraiths and changelings can draw on, and on a large map they come and go by doors the Storyteller marks.
